I1.quote: Searched the main text, figures and captions for a gravimetric, volumetric (Sieverts) or flow measurement of H2 uptake from the gas phase (isotherm, pressure change, microbalance, uptake per gram at a stated T and P) and found none. The only H quantity is the hydrogen content of the milled solid: "The hydrogen concentration in activated carbon hydrogenated by mechanical milling was estimated by inert gas fusion-thermal conductivity method." Hydrogen release is characterised by TDS alone.

I5.quote: We investigated the hydrogen adsorption / desorption properties of activated carbon that was prepared by mechanical milling in a hydrogen atmosphere at an ambient temperature.

notes: Borderline on I1. Activated carbon (Maxsorb) is milled in H2 (initial pressure 0.8 MPa, room temperature, 1-100 h; main p. 268, Section 2.1) and the resulting hydrogen concentration (about 2.6 wt.% gross, about 1.7 wt.% net of the 0.9 wt.% in the unmilled host; main p. 268, Section 3.2, Fig. 4) is determined afterwards by inert gas fusion-thermal conductivity analysis of the solid (HORIBA EMGA-621W), an elemental-analysis technique. No gravimetric, volumetric or flow uptake measurement is reported; the pressure during milling is only an initial value and no pressure record is given. The paper itself attributes part of the hydrogen to dangling-bond reaction and part to a KOH remnant. TDS (Section 3.4, Figs. 6-7) gives desorption peaks and activation energies, not an uptake value. Other criteria, had I1 been met: carbon sorbent yes (activated carbon); specific surface area reported in Fig. 3 (about 1200 m2/g host, about 400-600 m2/g after milling, BET at P/P0 < 0.06) and text of Section 3.1; I3 would rest on initial pressure 0.8 MPa and 'room temperature' without a number. Not retracted (record is_retracted false; no retraction notice in the PDF). Not a review, thesis or patent. No statement that the values were published before.
